tasks.goal: Port and verify the pinned Cordis Context, service registry, event modes, effect ownership, dependency injection, fiber activation, rollback, and quiescent disposal contract. Treat Loader and Include as optional consumers, not prerequisites of the Cordis core. This task is the single owner of the lifecycle change and ALL necessary boot/harness/CLI/HMR/diagnostics consumer adaptations. Follow .goose/cordis-lifecycle-contract.md. Preserve the retained round-six combined checkpoint, including its 49 modified files and existing event-order assertions; do not reimplement completed cases. Do not defer required consumer await/settlement changes to a separate task. Existing tests are not authority for loop-less synchronous activation: if retaining that adaptation, request a source-backed judge verdict. First inspect the combined checkpoint and run focused lifecycle tests, then close remaining concrete gaps. Full original Cordis acceptance remains required. Absorb the old activation-microtask-deferral proposal and readiness invariant source mapping into this owner; classify any genuinely Loader/Include composition-only cases with their existing owner and evidence, without deferring Cordis clauses. Judge arbitration (round seven) reconciled the conflicting proposals into this single owner: (1) preserve ordinary effect owner visibility until asynchronous cleanup settles (reference/vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:485-520) instead of retiring the wrapper before cleanup; (2) publish startup failure as LOADING -> UNLOADING -> FAILED while still unloading the effects collected before failure, removing the premature FAILED publication; (3) settle every Loader Entry/EntryGroup initialization, update, dependent fiber activation and teardown task before tree, boot, harness, CLI or HMR settlement returns. The proposed separate vendor/cordis-loader-settlement node is absorbed here, as the judge directed. The loop-less inline activation branch (python38-no-ambient-checkpoint) and the caller-driven awaitable disposal tail are permitted Python 3.8 adaptations; in-loop activation keeps the upstream deferral, cancellation and epoch-invalidation window. Scope arbitration of round seven: keep Loader EntryGroup.create data-rollback semantics in the existing vendor/loader task, not this core acceptance. Preserve the three completed lifecycle fixes. The only remaining core corrective action is to own the script-bridge scheduled root Fiber disposal task and join its completion plus dependent Fiber inertia before boot/harness/CLI/HMR settlement returns, including mid-startup root disposal. Add a strict no-pending-task/no-unawaited-coroutine regression. This preserves all existing core acceptance; it does not defer lifecycle shutdown.
